 GTA VI pre-loads push Virgin Media O2 network to record traffic high
 Downloads surpass previous records by 3.8 per cent and 4 per cent as gamers prepare for launch
 Published
 2 days ago on
 November 14, 2026 
 By
 indiantelevision.com Team 
 Follow us on Google News 
 Follow us on WhatsApp 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 MUMBAI: Vice City has not even opened its doors, but Grand Theft Auto VI is already causing a traffic jam – on the internet. The rush to pre-load Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated title sent Virgin Media O2’s broadband network to its busiest day on record on 10 November, with gamers downloading the game ahead of its scheduled 19 November release.
 The surge delivered two new milestones for the UK telecom operator: its highest-ever evening peak broadband traffic and its largest-ever daily data volume. The numbers suggest that the wait for GTA VI is being measured not just in years, but also in gigabytes.
 The latest evening peak surpassed the previous record, set on 5 May 2026 during the Champions League semi-final between Arsenal and Atlético Madrid, by 3.8 per cent. The record for total daily data consumption was also broken, with volumes exceeding the previous high, set on 1 November during the release of Fortnite Chapter 7 Mini Season, by 4 per cent.
 The scale of the rush became clear as the day unfolded. At 11.05 pm on 10 November, the total volume of data downloaded had already exceeded the previous record for an entire day. In other words, the network had crossed its earlier daily high before the day itself had even ended.
 The first wave of downloads was equally striking. Between midnight and 1 am on 10 November, broadband traffic rose 51.6 per cent compared with the same hour a week earlier, as pre-loading got under way. By 9 am, the cumulative volume of downloaded data was 73.3 per cent higher than during the equivalent period on 3 November.
 The figures underline the extraordinary anticipation surrounding GTA VI, which is due to arrive on 19 November. Pre-loading allows players to download the game before its official release, so they can begin playing without having to wait for a large download on launch day.
 But the preparations are not limited to internet connections. Virgin Media O2’s polling suggests that gamers are making room in their schedules and budgets for the release, with some treating launch week almost like a holiday.
 Nearly half (46 per cent) of surveyed players expect to download GTA VI before release day. Another 45 per cent expect to spend £50 or more on gaming equipment, excluding the cost of the game itself, indicating that the launch is prompting some players to upgrade their set-ups as well as clear space on their consoles.
 Time, meanwhile, appears to be the other big investment. More than three-quarters (78 per cent) of respondents have already made, or plan to make, changes to their schedules to find time to play.
 Almost a quarter (23 per cent) expect to stay up later than usual or sacrifice sleep, while 22 per cent plan to keep an entire weekend free. The commitment is even more pronounced among working respondents who expect to play: half (50 per cent) plan to take some time off work, with a third (33 per cent) expecting to take at least two days.
 That combination of pre-release downloads, equipment spending and diary reshuffling shows how a major game launch can spill beyond the gaming community and into the wider digital infrastructure supporting it.
 Virgin Media O2 chief technology officer Jeanie York said the game was already creating a record-breaking moment for the operator’s network, with fans downloading it in large numbers ahead of launch. She said the company had prepared its infrastructure for the demand associated with a release of this scale, while emphasising the importance of reliable broadband for players looking to get the game installed in time.
 For Virgin Media O2, the 10 November surge also offers a glimpse of how much data a major entertainment release can generate before consumers have even started using the product. Unlike a live sporting event, which drives a concentrated spike as viewers tune in, a game pre-load can trigger substantial download activity as players rush to get ready ahead of launch.
 With the release date approaching, the network has already had its biggest day. The next test will be whether launch day brings another wave of activity as players move from downloading the streets of Vice City to exploring them.
